text:
Seattle and Carolina play again two days after the Hurricanes beat the Kraken 4-1 in Seattle, a game our numbers say Carolina deserved to win 73% of the time. The Hurricanes have won three straight and are 4-1-0 in their last five, while the Kraken are 2-3-0 over that span. Both teams are missing a center: Jordan Staal (calf) for Carolina, Jared McCann (lower body) for Seattle. Jackson Blake has moved into Staal's spot beside Martinook and Ehlers, and Jordan Eberle has stepped in beside Beniers and Samoskevich.

Carolina has the edge in chance creation. At five on five the Hurricanes take 58% of the expected goals (the quality of shots each side gets), against 45% for Seattle, and our model projects 3.77 goals for Carolina against 2.38 for Seattle. Carolina's power play is also stronger, at 0.88 expected goals a game to Seattle's 0.56. In net, projected starter Pyotr Kochetkov is 9.8 goals saved above expected this season (how many more saves he's made than the shots predicted). Seattle's projected Joey Daccord is at -2.5, and he's .865 over his last five starts.

For Carolina, Sebastian Aho has a 37% chance to score and 76% to get a point, and Logan Stankoven carries a six-game point streak. For Seattle, Berkly Catton, drafted eighth overall in 2024, has 10 points in 10 games. Our under-the-radar pick is Carolina's Mark Jankowski: 3.9 expected goals in his last 10 games, and Daccord has allowed more than his shots deserved. We have him at 24% to score.
